name: Skinned Tom
description: Skinned Tom is a Southern American urban legend and cautionary tale about a man flayed alive after an adulterous affair, whose skinless, knife-carrying spirit now haunts lovers' lanes and remote roads as a warning against infidelity.
full_description: Skinned Tom is an urban legend and cautionary tale from the American South, with versions recorded in Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, and parts of Georgia. The core narrative involves a man — typically described as a charming womanizer or adulterer — who is discovered in an affair by a jealous husband or family member and is violently killed, typically by being flayed or skinned alive. His spirit returns as a humanoid figure entirely devoid of skin, exposing raw red musculature and sinew, typically carrying a long knife (either the blade used to flay him or a hunting knife taken from his killer). The creature haunts parked cars, motel parking lots, and remote roads at night, particularly locations associated with romantic trysts. The legend functions as an explicit moral warning: do not cheat on your partner, do not engage in secret affairs, and do not linger in isolated romantic spots after dark. Like many Southern Gothic cautionary legends, Skinned Tom combines lurid horror imagery with a strict moral framework, using the supernatural to enforce social norms around fidelity and discretion. The legend has limited documentation in academic folklore archives but has been transmitted orally through generations of Southern communities and appears in contemporary internet folklore discussions.
origin: The American South, with documented oral tradition in Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, and parts of Georgia.

etymology.origin: American South; oral tradition of unknown specific origin but documented in Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, and Georgia.
etymology.meaning: Tom is a generic male name serving as the protagonist; 'Skinned' refers to the flaying that creates the creature.
etymology.first_use: Oral tradition of uncertain age; documented in contemporary folklore surveys of the American South.

cultural_notes: Skinned Tom encodes a strict moral framework around fidelity and discretion. The horror of the skinless form is inseparable from the moral: the man who stripped away his moral cover (through adultery) has his physical cover (skin) stripped in kind. The punishment fits the crime in a literalized, grotesque moral equation.
